checks.assessment: confirmed invalid universal step; Major retained
checks.independent_reasoning: Source lines 850-875 (Proposition 5.1, printed p14) do not assume the complementary intersection I is nonzero. Independently checked the given T3 example: g inverse has 2x2 block [[1,a],[a,1]], third entry (1-a^2)^-1, a=(1/2)sin(2pi z); det(g)=1 and g eigenvalues <=2. dx and dy are harmonic, hence beta=*dy is harmonic, and dx wedge beta=a vol has zero integral but is not the zero form. Its primitive is -cos(2pi z)/(4pi) dx wedge dy. Thus no tau can satisfy vol(N) h(c1) wedge h(c2)=I(vol+d tau) when I=0. The actual maps f_j(u)=j u mod Z3 obey |Df_j|^3<=2sqrt(2)j^3 and Jac=j^3, so K=8 and A=omega3 j^3 meet the setup. This checks an admissible instance, not only an abstract zero-intersection algebra.
checks.counterevidence_and_severity: The proposition conclusion need not be false: the oscillating wedge coefficient converges weakly to zero. The correct cohomological identity is h(c1) wedge h(c2)=(I/vol(N))vol+d eta. Source Lemma 3.2, Proposition 4.2 and Theorem 4.4 supply the exact-form decay, wedge limit and normalized volume limit needed for repair. Theorem 4.4 explicitly chooses I nonzero; its separate use is not refuted. The defective step is in the core algebraic-limit proof, so Major is retained without claiming a false main theorem.

checks.assessment: confirmed unsupported theorem-scope extension; Major retained
checks.independent_reasoning: Read source 375-422 and Appendix B 1200-1225. Corollary 1.2 quantifies over closed smooth four-manifolds with a homeomorphism-type conclusion, whereas the construction before it gives the standard connected-sum smooth/PL representatives. Proposition B.1 requires compatible PL structures on both manifolds. A bare homeomorphism to an exotic smooth structure does not provide the needed quasiregular map or a compatible PL transport. Preserved primary arXiv:1707.03667v4 excerpts in web_evidence.json were read: Theorem 1.3 constructs covers of standard targets, Remark 1.4 explicitly distinguishes exotic counterparts, and Corollary 1.5 has direction exotic-to-standard, which cannot be inverted to supply the claimed sufficiency.
checks.counterevidence_and_severity: The necessary bound and ellipticity of standard representatives remain supported. No exotic counterexample, false necessity statement or present-day global open-problem claim is asserted. This is a missing argument for an advertised general application, not merely wording of an unused lemma; Major is retained. Restricting to compatible PL/smooth representatives repairs scope.

checks.independent_reasoning: Read Example 7.3, source 972-1002. Balls B(2^j e1,j) overlap at j=1,2 and j=2,3; the tail j>=3 is disjoint. With the printed positive zoom radius j/2 on B2, the annulus 1<|x|<2 survives and the actual map is H(x)=Qx for |x|<=1 and Q_(2-|x|)x outside. In dimension two with Q a pi/2 rotation, at (3/2,0) its derivative is R_(pi/4)[[1,0],[-3pi/4,1]], not Q. The radial skew-generator identity gives det(DH)=1, so normalization does not remove this difference.
checks.counterevidence_and_severity: Use j>=3 and positive scale j/4 to place all of B2 inside the rigid-rotation core; an identity zoom centered at -j^2 e1 with scale j avoids all supports. Uniform twist bounds persist, and the desired distinct limits can be obtained. The main proof is independent of this example, so Minor is retained.
